explanation: ENORMOUS means extremely large, which is huge. Heavy is about weight, not size.
To assist is to help. Watch, teach and follow are different actions.
To choose one item from many is to select it. Refuse is the opposite, and collect and gather do not involve picking one.
To shout is to cry out loudly, which is to yell. Whisper is the opposite, and argue and sing are different activities.
To purchase is to buy. Sell is the opposite, and borrow and steal do not involve paying.
Silent means making no sound, which is quiet. Calm means peaceful, which is not necessarily soundless.
To frighten someone is to scare them. Warn, chase and hurt are other actions.
A journey is a trip from one place to another. A route is the path taken, not the travel itself.
To reply is to answer. Ask is the opposite action.
CLEVER means mentally sharp, which is intelligent. Quick describes speed and careful describes attention.
EXHAUSTED means completely tired out. Weak, hungry and angry are other conditions.
FURIOUS means extremely angry, which is enraged. Puzzled, hurt and restless are other feelings.
PRECIOUS means of great value, which is valuable. A thing can be beautiful, ancient or scarce without being highly valued.
To obtain something is to get it, which is to acquire it. Offer, return and search are different actions.
To stroll is to walk slowly and easily. Run and hurry are faster, and climb is a different movement.
DELIGHTED means very happy, which is pleased. Surprised, relieved and amused are narrower feelings.
A hazard is a source of danger, which is a risk. Damage and accident are results, and a warning is a signal.
To discover something is to find it. Invent means to make something new, and lose is the opposite.
COURAGEOUS means showing courage, which is brave. Careless, strong and proud are different qualities.
To construct a bridge is to build it. Plan, paint and measure are other activities.
To abandon a place or a person is to leave them completely. Forgetting and losing are not deliberate acts of leaving.
NUMEROUS means great in number, which is many. Large refers to size.
To alter a plan is to change it. Repeat, measure and remove are other actions.
To remain in a place is to stay in it. Return means to go back, and wait and rest are not the same.
An aim is a goal, the thing one is trying to achieve. A plan is the method and effort is the work.
To hurry is to move or act quickly, which is to rush. Stumble, worry and follow are other actions.
The border of a country or field is its edge. A corner is a single point, and a wall is a built structure.
OBVIOUS means easily seen or understood, which is clear. Simple and common do not mean easily seen.
A mistake is an error. An accident is something unplanned and may not involve a wrong choice.
To reside in a city is to live there. Visit, work and sleep do not mean making a home.
To defend is to protect from harm. Attack is the opposite, and argue and escape are different actions.
To annoy someone is to irritate them. Confuse, frighten and question are different effects.
An amicable meeting is friendly. Polite, formal and calm describe manners and mood, not friendship.
To anticipate an event is to expect it. Fear and doubt are feelings, and preparing is an action.
ARDUOUS means requiring great effort, which is strenuous. Lengthy, boring and risky describe other features of a task.
A bleak future offers little hope, which is dismal. Empty, cold and silent describe other features.
A cautious person is careful about danger, which is wary. Timid means shy, and slow and serious do not mean careful.
A concise report says much in few words, which is brief. Simple, plain and accurate describe other qualities.
A conspicuous object is easy to see, which is noticeable. Important, famous and unusual are not about being seen.
A cordial welcome is warm and friendly. Polite and formal describe manners, which may be present without warmth.
CRUCIAL means of the greatest importance, which is vital. Urgent concerns time, and useful is a weaker idea.
A deliberate act is done on purpose, which is intentional. Careless and sudden suggest the opposite, and clever describes skill, not intention.
A dilemma is a difficult situation in which every option has a cost, which is a predicament. It is not a mistake or an argument.
A dispute is a disagreement, which is a quarrel. Promise, decision and failure are not forms of disagreement between people.
A durable material stays in good condition for a long time, which is lasting. Heavy, valuable and plain do not mean long-lasting.
An eminent scientist is famous and respected in his field, which is distinguished. Elderly, wealthy and popular do not mean respected.
To endeavour to do something is to try hard to do it, which is to attempt. Succeed describes the result of trying.
An enigma is something hard to understand, which is a puzzle. A secret is merely hidden, and disaster and failure are different ideas.
A feasible plan can be carried out, which is possible. Profitable, sensible and likely are different judgements.
To fortify a wall is to make it stronger. Decorate and enlarge change appearance or size, and discard is to throw away.
To hinder progress is to obstruct it. Assist is the opposite, and avoid and blame are different actions.
An impartial judge favours neither side, which is unbiased. Silent, polite and careful do not describe fairness.
An inevitable event cannot be avoided. Likely only means probable, so it is weaker.
To lament a loss is to mourn it with open grief. Recall, announce and accept do not express sorrow.
A legitimate claim is allowed by law, which is lawful. Honest, fair and popular describe other qualities.
An obsolete machine is no longer used because newer ones have replaced it, which is outdated. Worn, ancient and unusual do not explain why it is no longer used.
To persevere is to keep going despite difficulty, which is to persist. Struggle describes the difficulty, not the continuation.
A plausible excuse seems reasonable and likely to be true, which is believable. Popular, honest and useful describe other things.
A prevalent belief is accepted by many people, which is widespread. Rising, serious and recent do not describe how far something extends.
The primary reason is the main one, which is the chief reason. Final, simple and ordinary do not mean most important.
A radiant smile shines with happiness, which is bright. Warm, beautiful and calm are different qualities.
A reckless driver acts without thought of danger, which is rash. Bold has a positive sense, and restless and cruel describe other things.
Remorse is deep sorrow for a wrong one has done, which is regret. Fear, envy and anger are different feelings.
To scrutinise a document is to examine it closely. Remember, summarise and suspect are different mental acts.
A serene lake is calm and peaceful. Silent, empty and happy do not capture the quality of calm.
Sporadic gunfire comes now and then, which is occasional. Regular is the opposite, and rapid and violent describe speed and force.
A unanimous vote has everyone in agreement, which is undivided. Popular and public mean liked or open, not complete agreement.
A vigilant guard keeps careful watch, which is watchful. Brave, serious and silent are other qualities.
To withhold payment is to hold it back, which is to retain it. Release and donate mean giving it up, and delay only postpones it.
An abundant harvest is large in quantity, which is plentiful. Useful and common do not describe quantity, and rich describes quality.
An ambiguous sentence can be understood in more than one way, which is unclear. False and difficult are different problems.
An absurd idea is foolish to the point of being ridiculous. Shocking, impossible and funny describe other qualities.
To deceive is to cause someone to believe something false, which is to mislead. Persuade, tempt and offend do not involve falsehood.
To disperse a crowd is to scatter it in different directions. Disappear and depart do not mean spreading out.
To mingle is to mix with others. Gather, meet and join do not describe the blending together.
A perplexed student is confused, which is puzzled. Worried, surprised and annoyed are different feelings.
A spontaneous cheer arises without planning, which is unplanned. Sudden concerns speed, and cheerful and eager concern mood.
To thrive is to grow vigorously and succeed, which is to flourish. Survive only means to stay alive.
To tolerate something is to bear it without protest, which is to endure it. Forgive and approve are stronger, and ignore does not suggest bearing something unpleasant.
To astonish is to surprise greatly, which is to amaze. Frighten, confuse and please are other effects.
ACRIMONY is sharp, bitter ill feeling, especially in speech, which is bitterness. Violence, rivalry and sorrow are different things.
To alleviate pain is to make it easier to bear, which is to relieve it. Remove is stronger because it takes pain away entirely.
To ameliorate conditions is to make them better, which is to improve them. Repair, alter and correct do not necessarily mean making things better.
An anomaly is a departure from what is normal or expected, which is an irregularity. A mistake is a wrong action, and ruin and rarity are different ideas.
AUSTERE describes a strict, severe manner, which is stern. Wealthy, cheerful and clever describe other qualities.
A belligerent person is eager to pick a fight, which is aggressive. Angry, loud and proud do not describe the same eagerness for conflict.
A circumspect person considers all possible consequences before acting, which is cautious. Secretive, reserved and suspicious are different attitudes.
A complacent person is pleased with himself and sees no need to improve, which is self-satisfied. Lazy, selfish and careless are different faults.
To debilitate is to make feeble, which is to weaken. Injure, punish and delay are different effects.
To disparage someone's work is to speak of it as having little value, which is to belittle it. Disagree, accuse and ignore are not the same.
An erudite scholar has deep knowledge from study, which is learned. Clever, famous and polite do not depend on study.
To exacerbate a problem is to make it worse. Spread, reveal and prolong do not necessarily involve worsening.
To expedite a process is to make it go faster, which is to hasten it. Improve, complete and permit are different results.
A fastidious eater is hard to please, which is fussy. Clean, humble and proud are different qualities.
Fortuitous means happening by chance, which is accidental. A sudden or unusual event need not happen by chance.
An innocuous remark does no harm, which is harmless. Obscure, gentle and boring do not mean without harm.
To obfuscate is to make something unclear and hard to understand, which is to confuse. Reveal is the opposite, and distort and delay are different.
PERNICIOUS means causing serious harm, often gradually, which is harmful. Contagious, subtle and painful are narrower qualities.
To placate an angry man is to calm him, which is to pacify him. Reward, persuade and excuse are different actions.
A pristine forest remains in its original condition, which is unspoiled. Ancient, fragile and bright do not suggest that nothing has touched it.
To finish a task is to complete it. Begin is the opposite, and repeat and delay are different actions.
To mend a broken chair is to repair it. Break is the opposite, and clean and paint do not fix damage.
To request is to ask politely. Order is a command, and reply and refuse are different actions.
ADEQUATE means enough for the purpose, which is sufficient. Excellent is far better than enough, and ordinary and modest describe quality or size.
To defer a meeting is to postpone it to a later time. Cancel and refuse end it, and reduce changes its size.
An eloquent speaker expresses ideas fluently and persuasively, which is articulate. Forceful and confident describe manner, not skill with words.
A momentous decision has great importance, which is significant. Sudden, public and rare are not about importance.
To neglect a duty is to fail to give it attention, which is to ignore it. Inspect is the opposite of neglect, and damage and reject are different.
An obstacle is something that blocks the way, which is a barrier. Danger, delay and question are not physical or direct blocks.
A sceptical listener doubts what he is told, which is doubtful. Puzzled, angry and careful are different attitudes.
Subsequent events are those that come afterwards, which are following events. Earlier is the opposite, and final means last of all.
An accurate measurement is exact. Careful describes the person, honest the intention, and recent the time.
A harsh punishment is very strict, which is severe. Cold, loud and unfair describe other qualities.
A cogent argument is clear and logical in a way that persuades, which is convincing. Clever, brief and lengthy do not capture persuasion by logic.
A laudable effort deserves praise, which is praiseworthy. Ambitious, popular and successful do not say that it deserves praise.
